model.name: Unified WebItem scenario unit (bookmark / .url / .webloc)
model.description: A dropped URL of any scheme becomes ONE unified ior:class:WebItem scenario unit - a single model that plays the role of a Google bookmark (drag-droppable), a Windows .url file, and a macOS .webloc. Model: { uuid, name (page title/bookmark name), description, icon (favicon), badge (scheme icon), url (the actual URL, any scheme), scheme (http/mailto/tel/maps/calshow/...), parentFolder (ior ref to parent folder unit), children[] (folder hierarchy) }. Dropped URLs create WebItem units (not bare text/uri-list files); the preview renders the scheme launcher card (v0.6.87) with name+icon+badge; Open-in-New-Tab does window.open(url) which hands scheme URLs to the native app; WebItems organise into folders (parent/children like the file tree); and they import from .url (Windows INI), .webloc (macOS plist), and Google bookmarks HTML.
model.tronQuote: > TRON: "create a scenario WebItem for URLs that acts like a Google bookmark (drag-droppable), a .url file (Windows), and a .webloc (Mac) - unified as ONE ior:class:WebItem unit."

acceptanceCriteria.text: ior:class:WebItem has model fields: uuid, name, description, icon (favicon), badge (scheme icon), url, scheme, parentFolder (ior ref), children[].
Dropped URLs create WebItem units, NOT bare text/uri-list files.
The preview renders the scheme launcher card (v0.6.87) with name + icon + badge.
Open-in-New-Tab does window.open(url) so the native app handles the scheme URL.
WebItems organise into folders via parentFolder/children[] (parent/children like the file tree).
Import from Windows .url (INI format) yields WebItem units.
Import from macOS .webloc (plist) yields WebItem units.
Import from Google bookmarks HTML yields WebItem units with folder hierarchy preserved.
